title: G-PARC: Graph-Physics Aware Recurrent Convolutional neural networks for spatiotemporal dynamics on unstructured meshes

key_results: G-PARC achieves 2–3× fewer parameters than MeshGraphNet/MeshGraphKAN; outperforms on nonlinear benchmarks (hydrology, shock waves, elastoplasticity); generalizes across spatial/temporal discretizations and handles moving meshes
comments: Embedding analytical differential operators into GNN graph via moving least squares is elegant; recurrent vs. transformer trade-off characterized, though multi-step error accumulation not thoroughly analyzed.

model_io.model: Graph-Physics Aware Recurrent Convolutional Network (G-PARC) with MLS kernels

hypotheses.hypothesis: Analytical MLS-based differential operators embedded in GNN outperform learned encoder-processor-decoder on nonlinear PDE benchmarks
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; superior accuracy and parameter efficiency on hydrology, shock, and plasticity problems

title: Energy transfer and dynamic response of a gasbag-driven confined granular bed
task: Characterize energy transfer and particle dynamics in gasbag-driven confined granular media
key_results: Particle velocity increases with driving pressure (0.2–3.0 MPa) but decreases nonlinearly with particle diameter beyond critical size; Janssen-like stress redistribution dominates at larger diameters
comments: DEM-FEM model captures both pressure-driven inertial dispersion and contact-constrained regime transition; results suggest design optimization for granular impact applications.

model_io.model: DEM-FEM coupled simulation with experimental validation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Response transitions from inertia-dominated dispersion (small particles) to contact-constrained motion (large particles) with increased wall friction
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; nonlinear velocity decrease with diameter attributed to enhanced particle–particle contacts and Janssen-type stress redistribution

title: Design and development of a 1-bit dual-mode metasurface for sub-6 GHz wireless communication systems
task: Design 1-bit dual-mode metasurface for sub-6 GHz wireless beamforming
key_results: 180° ± 20° phase shift across bandwidth; insertion loss 0.4 dB (transmission) / 0.21 dB (reflection) at center frequency; 3 dB bandwidth 16% (Tx) / 12% (Rx); ±60° beam steering with 6 dB gain enhancement
comments: Fixed stripline prototype simplifies fabrication vs. diode switching; 12% reflective bandwidth is notably narrower than transmission—impedance matching trade-off is noted but not analyzed.

model_io.model: 1-bit dual-mode metasurface unit cell with stripline phase configuration

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fixed stripline configuration replicates diode switching behavior while reducing cost and complexity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; phase-switching logic validated experimentally with good agreement to simulation

title: Tuning light-matter interaction of near-infrared nanoplasmonic scintillators
task: Enhance near-infrared scintillator brightness via nanoplasmonic light-matter coupling
key_results: Graphene antennas achieve strong-coupling signatures at g = 8 meV with κ = 3.5 meV linewidth; narrow-band emitters show most favorable conditions for coherent-exchange phenomena
comments: Framework is computational; experimental validation on actual scintillator-antenna systems would strengthen claims about radiation detection applicability.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Graphene's ultranarrow linewidth enables strong coupling at lower coupling strengths than broadband antennas
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; graphene shows observable coherent signatures at g = 8 meV vs higher thresholds for other platforms

title: Analysis of dose reconstruction techniques in pre-treatment QA of large-field RapidArc technique with a 2D detector array
task: Assess dose reconstruction methods for large-field pelvic RapidArc pre-treatment QA
key_results: Global normalization: 3D GPR >95% with <2% difference between methods; local normalization: composite shows −11.6% lower GPR at 1 mm/2%, <2% at 3 mm/3%
comments: Composite reconstruction enables full-field verification without sacrificing accuracy under practical criterion (3 mm/3%), improving clinical workflow.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Composite reconstruction (merged longitudinally-shifted measurements) produces equivalent dosimetric accuracy to standard single measurement
hypotheses.result: Confirmed under global normalization; local normalization shows criterion-dependent differences

title: Phase transition and optical bistability in a cold Rydberg Rb sample observed via absorption spectroscopy
task: Investigate optical bistability and phase transitions in cold Rydberg atom ensembles
key_results: Hysteretic behavior observed for n = 43–77; bistability signatures consistent with Rydberg blockade-induced cold plasma; characteristic state-transition dynamics revealed
comments: Experimental demonstration of collective nonlinear optical response via many-body Rydberg interactions; mechanism aligns with theoretical predictions but detailed temperature/density characterization would clarify plasma formation.

model_io.model: Cold ⁸⁵Rb Rydberg ensemble with absorption spectroscopy

hypotheses.hypothesis: Rydberg blockade induces cold plasma formation, generating optical bistability via collective many-body interactions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; observed hysteretic behavior and transition dynamics consistent with blockade-driven plasma picture

title: Ultrahigh spatiotemporal resolution terahertz scanning tunnelling microscopy
task: Enable atomic-scale ultrafast spectroscopy via terahertz scanning tunneling microscopy
key_results: Simultaneous atomic spatial (<1 Å) and sub-picosecond temporal resolution; access to electron dynamics, molecular motions, and many-body states; potential for Floquet engineering and light-induced superconductivity studies
comments: Comprehensive review synthesizing STM and THz physics; future directions (non-equilibrium quantum topology, optical control of pairing) are speculative but motivate further development.

model_io.model: Terahertz STM junction with picosecond pulse injection

title: Engineering topolectrical circuits
task: Review engineering principles and applications of topolectrical circuits
key_results: Topological band theory translated to wiring-defined electrical networks; defect tolerance, directional flow, boundary amplification demonstrated; cross-disciplinary uses in quantum simulation, AI design, curved-space geometries identified
comments: Comprehensive review spanning physics, engineering applications, and emerging integration (memristive devices, co-design); good balance of fundamental concepts and practical deployment routes, though some applications remain preliminary.

title: Effects of magnon-magnon interactions on the magnon spectrum of 2D altermagnets
task: Calculate magnon-magnon interaction effects on 2D altermagnet magnon spectrum
key_results: Continuous similarity transformation yields one-magnon dispersion and magnon-magnon interaction corrections; roton minimum size and altermagnetic spin splitting quantified; transformation divergencies signal Néel order breakdown or magnon decay
comments: Methodologically rigorous application of similarity transformation to altermagnets; divergence analysis identifies physical limits of perturbative treatment, though numerical phase diagram could strengthen predictions.

model_io.model: Spin-1/2 Heisenberg altermagnet on square lattice with similarity transformation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Magnon-magnon interactions modify dispersion beyond single-magnon picture; altermagnetic spin splitting survives interactions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; interaction corrections calculated; spin splitting behavior characterized

title: Verification of training and compensation under variations: simulation and measurement on oxide semiconductor analog in-memory computing chips
task: Validate variation-aware training and noise compensation in oxide-semiconductor analog in-memory computing
key_results: Optimal combination of training and inference noise intensity improves accuracy on fabricated chips; positive correlation between chip inherent noise and optimal training noise; variation-aware training superior to Dropout in some regimes
comments: First experimental validation on actual oxide-semiconductor AiMC hardware; correlation between chip noise and training noise is practical insight, but sample size and statistical significance not clearly reported.

model_io.model: Oxide-semiconductor analog in-memory computing chip with noise injection

hypotheses.hypothesis: Training noise intensity should match chip inherent noise for optimal accuracy
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; positive correlation observed across multiple chips

title: An efficient probabilistic hardware architecture for diffusion-like models
task: Design energy-efficient probabilistic hardware for diffusion model inference
key_results: All-transistor stochastic computer implementing denoising models at hardware level; ~10,000× lower energy than GPUs on simple image benchmark while maintaining performance parity
comments: Extraordinary energy efficiency claim requires independent verification on broader benchmarks; unclear how design scales to complex models or batch processing.

model_io.model: All-transistor probabilistic hardware for diffusion models

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hardware-native stochastic computation for denoising achieves GPU-competitive performance at drastically reduced energy
hypotheses.result: Indicated on simple image benchmark; generalization to realistic models not demonstrated

title: Optical spiking neural networks via rogue-wave statistics
task: Implement spiking neural networks using optical rogue-wave statistics for thresholding
key_results: Phase-engineered caustics enable sparse optical spikes via rogue-wave criterion; BreastMNIST 82.45%, Olivetti Faces 96.67% accuracy; energy efficiency gains over digital neural networks
comments: Innovative use of extreme-value statistics for optical nonlinearity; physics-informed digital twin co-design is practical, though energy metrics vs. GPUs and scaling to larger networks remain unaddressed.

model_io.model: Optical spiking neural network with phase-engineered caustics and rogue-wave thresholding

hypotheses.hypothesis: Optical rogue-wave statistics provide programmable nonlinear thresholding suitable for neuromorphic inference
hypotheses.result: Confirmed on BreastMNIST and Olivetti Faces; competitive accuracy achieved

title: An atlas of primate insular cortex reveals a signal-processing strategy in von Economo neurons
task: Characterize neural cell types and signal-processing strategies in primate anterior insular cortex
key_results: Resolved 78 cell types in macaque AIC; identified two VEN subtypes (DSG2+ VEN-L and POC5+ VEN-S) with distinct projection patterns; discovered dendrite-originating axon geometry enhances somatic responsiveness to deep-layer inputs
comments: The multimodal integration of transcriptomics and electrophysiology is powerful, though the functional significance of the identified signal-processing strategy for integrating interoceptive/exteroceptive information remains to be demonstrated behaviorally.

hypotheses.hypothesis: VENs exhibit specialized signal-processing through dendrite-originating axon geometry
hypotheses.result: Axon geometry reshapes action potential dynamics and enhances somatic responsiveness to deep-layer synaptic inputs
